how_to_apply: Open the application link, which is available only on www.highcourtchd.gov.in.
Read the detailed employment notice before filling in the form.
Use a valid personal email address and mobile number, because recruitment updates are sent there. Do not change them after registration.
Fill in all details, including the category. No change is allowed after submission.
Upload a recent passport size photograph (not more than 30 days old, white background) and your signatures. An application without a proper photograph and signature will be rejected.
Upload scanned copies of any FIR or conviction/acquittal orders, and the document claiming fee relaxation as a dependent of Ex-Servicemen, if these apply to you.
Re-check your details and pay the fee through a facility such as internet banking or a debit/credit card.
Keep printed copies of the form, and keep five copies of the uploaded photograph for later stages.
A candidate may submit only one application for a particular category. If more than one is submitted, only the latest will be considered.

Keep the application printout with proof of qualification, date of birth, caste certificate and any NOC. The annexures are in the notice, and Annexures III, IV and V must be attested by a Notary Public.

Regular government employees must obtain the NOC when applying and keep it with them. Failure to produce the original when required cancels the candidature. Contract or ad hoc workers in government offices apply as non-departmental candidates.

content_sections.heading: Punjab and Haryana High Court Chowkidar Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Applicants of all categories should be not less than 18 years and not more than 35 years as on 21 November 2026. For Ex-Servicemen, the upper age limit is relaxed by the number of years of their defence service plus 03 years. Only two documents are accepted as proof of date of birth: the Matriculation Certificate from a recognized Education Board, for candidates who are matriculate or above, or the Birth Certificate from the Registrar of Births and Deaths, for those qualified below Matric. Minimum Middle Standard and maximum 10+2 from a recognized School Education Board or recognized School. All eligibility conditions must be met on the last date of online submission. Candidates must also give an affidavit that they are not qualified above 10+2. Concealing a higher qualification can lead to criminal action and termination from service. SC/ST/BC reservation and fee relaxation are only for candidates holding a certificate from Punjab, Haryana or U.T. Chandigarh who are also domiciled or permanent residents there. SC/ST/BC applicants from other areas or states must apply under General Category. BC candidates must not fall in the creamy layer, and their certificate must be the latest one. Reservation, fee and age relaxation under the Ex-Servicemen category are for Ex-Servicemen themselves, not their dependents. No man who has more than one wife living, and no woman married to a man already having a wife living, is eligible for appointment. See the official notification for the full eligibility conditions for the post of Chowkidar.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Candidates are selected on their performance in the interview. Depending on the number of applications, any suitable shortlisting criterion can be followed, and candidates will be told about it at the appropriate time. Meeting the eligibility criteria does not by itself entitle an applicant to an interview call. The date, time and venue of the interview will be published on the High Court website. Original documents will be checked at testimonials checking. The E-Admit Card link for provisionally eligible candidates will be uploaded on the website, and candidates will also receive an email or SMS. Admit cards are not sent by post. Paste a photograph on the E-Admit Card, attested by a Gazetted Officer or self-attested. It must match the one uploaded with the application, or entry to the venue will be refused. Mobile phones, other electronic devices, watches, ornaments and other baggage are not allowed in the interview center. No TA/DA is paid for any stage of the recruitment process.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The posts are on the establishment of the High Court at Chandigarh. Duty hours may extend beyond normal working hours and even at odd hours.

Failure to produce the original when required cancels the candidature. Contract or ad hoc workers in government offices apply as non-departmental candidates. faq.question: Q1. Can a graduate apply for the Chowkidar post?
faq.answer: No. The maximum qualification is 10+2, and applicants with anything higher are not eligible.

faq.question: Q2. How many Chowkidar posts are open to General Category candidates?
faq.answer: 19 of the 22 posts are in the General Category, though the total may change by the time the merit list is prepared.

faq.question: Q3. I am an SC candidate from outside Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh. Which category do I choose?
faq.answer: You must apply under General Category and pay the General fee of Rs. 700.

faq.question: Q4. What is the interview marked on?
faq.answer: Half of the 50 marks are for suitability to the job and half are for etiquettes/manners.

faq.question: Q5. How much age relaxation do Ex-Servicemen get?
faq.answer: Their upper age limit rises by their years of defence service plus 03 years.

faq.question: Q6. Can I correct my application after submitting it?
faq.answer: No. Particulars, including the category, cannot be changed once filled, so check them before paying because the fee is not refunded.

faq.question: Q7. Will the High Court post my admit card?
faq.answer: No. You download the E-Admit Card from the High Court website after the link is uploaded and you receive an email or SMS about it.

faq.question: Q8. I work in a government department. What must I submit?
faq.answer: You need a Forwarding Letter/NOC in the Annexure II format from your Head of Department. The High Court may also seek a fresh NOC when giving the offer of appointment.

faq.question: Q9. Which version applies if a newspaper advertisement differs?
faq.answer: The contents on the official High Court website prevail over any advertisement published in newspapers.
